chunks: And it is reported by Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah. Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the man who suffers from a nosebleed while he is in prayer, so he said: If he is able to use water that is near him, on his right or left or in front of him, and he is facing the Qiblah, let him wash it off him, then let him pray whatever remains of his prayer; and if he is not able to use water until he turns away with his face or speaks, then his prayer has been broken.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer if one has a nosebleed during it?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the prominent chain of al-Kulayni, establishes the jurisprudential principle that minor impurities (najasah) do not invalidate prayer if they can be removed without disrupting the prayer's continuity. It highlights the Shia emphasis on practical ease (yusr), distinguishing between the physical act of washing and the cognitive or physical breaks (like turning the face or speaking) that sever the prayer's validity.
